condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: In humans, the ribonucleoside analog viramidine has an absolute oral bioavailability of 66.1%, showing that a polar ribose-heterocycle scaffold can achieve F well above 20%.
Purine nucleoside analog didanosine, despite acid lability and polar structure, shows absolute oral bioavailability values of 22-43% across doses and formulations, all above the 20% threshold.

Other nucleoside reverse-transcriptase inhibitors with similarly polar nucleoside structures show high absolute oral bioavailability: lamivudine 69-87%, zalcitabine 80%, zidovudine 61%, and stavudine 61-78%.
No L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F below 20% for any nucleoside analog context; the lowest reported values (didanosine 22-29%) remain above the threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
The query's N-amino ribosyl linkage is not represented in any L1 context, so acid stability, transporter affinity, and first-pass behavior of that specific linkage are unmeasured.
No query-specific data on nucleoside transporter involvement, efflux, or first-pass metabolism are available.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high (F >= 20%) because all transferable L1 nucleoside-analog contexts show absolute oral bioavailability above 20% (didanosine 22-43%, lamivudine 69-87%, zalcitabine 80%, zidovudine 61%, stavudine 61-78%, viramidine 66.1%), and no affirmative evidence supports F < 20%. The physicochemical low-permeability prior is not sufficient to override consistent analog endpoint evidence, though confidence is moderate because the query's N-amino ribosyl modification is not directly covered.
